# Given values (in thousands of dollars)
Q1 = 4807819  # Total collections Jan 1960
Q2 = 11893553 # Total collections Mar 1960
P1 = 26461    # Unemployment insurance Jan 1960
P2 = 20174    # Unemployment insurance Mar 1960

# Calculate changes
delta_Q = Q2 - Q1
delta_P = P2 - P1

print(f"ΔQ = {Q2} - {Q1} = {delta_Q}")
print(f"ΔP = {P2} - {P1} = {delta_P}")

print(f"\nArc elasticity = ({delta_Q}/{delta_P}) × (({P1}+{P2})/({Q1}+{Q2}))")
print(f"               = {delta_Q/delta_P:.6f} × ({(P1+P2)}/{(Q1+Q2)})")
print(f"               = {delta_Q/delta_P:.6f} × {(P1+P2)/(Q1+Q2):.10f}")
print(f"\nArc elasticity = {arc_elasticity:.3f}")
EOF

I have computed the arc elasticity of total IRS collections with respect to unemployment insurance contributions.

## Summary

**Data from Treasury Bulletin (June 1960):**
- **January 1960:** Total collections = 4,807,819 (thousands), Unemployment insurance = 26,461 (thousands)
- **March 1960:** Total collections = 11,893,553 (thousands), Unemployment insurance = 20,174 (thousands)

**Arc Elasticity Calculation:**
$$\varepsilon = \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta P} \times \frac{P_1 + P_2}{Q_1 + Q_2}$$

$$\varepsilon = \frac{7,085,734}{-6,287} \times \frac{26,461 + 20,174}{4,807,819 + 11,893,553}$$

$$\varepsilon = -1,127.045 \times 0.002792$$

$$\varepsilon = -3.147$$

The final answer **-3.147** has been written to `/app/answer.txt`.
